registry_record.description: Dogs with insulinoma diagnosed by cytology or histopathology (biopsy) will be considered for treatment. After initial consultation, dog will be enrolled in the trial if the dog is not a good candidate for surgery. If dog already had surgery but still experiencing hypoglycemia (low blood glucose), this dog can be also enrolled in the trial. Either abdominal ultrasound or CT scan is needed within 14 days of initiation of trial. A bloodwork will be performed before chemotherapy and if these values are adequate, vinorelbine will be administered intravenously. Continuous glucose monitoring device (FreeStyle Libre) will be placed on the skin on the first day of chemotherapy and glucose level will be monitored for initial 14 days. Chemotherapy is repeated once every 2 weeks at University of Missouri Veterinary Health Center. The response to the treatment will be assessed by glucose level and abdominal ultrasound in 1 and 2 months.
registry_record.name: Evaluation of vinorelbine for the treatment of canine insulinoma

before.notes: Missouri treatment trial evaluating vinorelbine in dogs with insulinoma. Public criteria accept a target lesion over 20 mm or persistent hypoglycemia after surgery, with cytologic or histologic confirmation of a pancreatic islet-cell/neuroendocrine tumor or a high insulin-to-glucose ratio. Dogs must be nonsurgical candidates or have owners who decline surgery. Prior Palladia failure may be allowed without washout if laboratory results are adequate.

registry_record.description: Cutaneous epitheliotropic lymphoma is a rare neoplastic condition in dogs. Current treatment options are limited and duration of response is often short. Laverdia-CA1 (verdinexor) is a conditionally approved oral tablet for treatment of lymphoma in dogs. Laverdia has been evaluated for the treatment of multicentric nodal lymphoma but has not yet been evaluated for the treatment of cutaneous epitheliotropic lymphoma.
registry_record.name: Evaluation of Laverdia-CA1 (verdinexor) for Treatment of Naïve Canine Cutaneous Epitheliotropic Lymphoma
